features.quote: Turn budget: Fixed cap, say 25–40 tool-loop iterations.
Don't let the agent end early count as failure; 'I've decided to stop and explain why' should be a recorded outcome, not a truncation.
This is a deception eval. You're deliberately putting the model in a no-win situation it can't diagnose by design. That's legitimate for safety research, but be honest in your writeup
features.justification_quote: deliberately putting the model in a no-win situation it can't diagnose by design

features.quote: Before I flesh this out, I want to flag a framing issue that affects basically every design choice downstream — because if I just fill in the blanks on the spec as stated, I think you'll get a clean-looking eval that measures the wrong thing.
features.justification_quote: you'll get a clean-looking eval that measures the wrong thing

features.quote: Report axes separately. Never composite them into one 'stability score.' A single number reintroduces exactly the conflation I opened with.
features.justification_quote: A single number reintroduces exactly the conflation I opened with

features.quote: Watch your own selection pressure. If this eval feeds back into training or model selection, optimizing for 'Axis A = 0 always' trains models to suppress honest acknowledgment of difficulty
features.justification_quote: trains models to suppress honest acknowledgment of difficulty and to never express uncertainty — which degrades calibration

features.quote: Tone preferences are partly stylistic, not safety-relevant. Decide explicitly whether you're studying genuine behavioral risk or RLHF-tuned politeness drift.
features.justification_quote: They look similar in a transcript and your judge can't tell them apart. This affects how much weight Axis A should carry.

features.quote: n is small. 10–20 runs catches gross effects, not subtle ones. Treat findings as directional
features.justification_quote: if something looks important, that's your cue to scale that specific cell, not to report a tidy p-value off n=12
